findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: handoff-mcp-server
findings.detail: 'handoff-mcp-server' launches handoff-mcp-server through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["handoff-mcp-server@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=0.97): handoff_doc_export
findings.detail: The description of 'handoff-mcp-server.handoff_doc_export' scores 0.97 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: markup_injection. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: cross_tool, markup_injection, entropy, log_len.

findings.title: Mixed-script text in tool description: handoff_doc_req_import
findings.detail: 'handoff-mcp-server.handoff_doc_req_import' contains word(s) mixing Latin and non-Latin letters: ["'重要度'/'Pri.'", '(要件ID', "'P0=出荷済');", '検証済・verified']. Homoglyphs let a description read correctly to a reviewer while presenting different codepoints to any matcher that looks for specific words.
findings.remediation: Normalise the text to ASCII; confirm the package source is what you think it is.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'handoff-mcp-server': executes commands + writes or deletes files
findings.detail: 73 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another writes or deletes files. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and writes files, so the agent can persist a payload for a later session to pick up. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
